limitations: The finite query ownership case uses two service identities, two adapter identities and two query slots for one agent. TaskScheduler retains the dirty-agent and dispatch model.
The adapter owner may be absent from the queried service identities. Runtime.close fences and drains its exact adapter while preserving a different active adapter.
Per-service worker and preflight drainage are covered separately by TaskRetirement. A hung adapter call cannot satisfy the stated progress assumption.

Real PGlite conformance checks delayed queries, stale query failure, unregister and adapter-owner closure across two runtimes. Multiple agents per batch and host reopening of retired adapters remain outside this model. Agent runtime-lifecycle models the host-confirmed physical alias handoff separately and binds real shared PGlite handle conformance. Core never inspects physical connections.
